requirements.evidence: All contract items are present: CreateQueue signature/normalization (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:16-28), UpdateQueue's nullable named arguments (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:20-26), SetQueueAccess (app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:23-72), QueuePermission::Call (app/Enums/QueuePermission.php:6), the QueueAccess model/factory/migration (app/Models/QueueAccess.php:11-32, database/factories/QueueAccessFactory.php:24-32, database/migrations/2026_10_29_032643_create_queue_access_table.php:14-21), and QueuePolicy (app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php:20-44) wired into CallNextTicket (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:32) and Ticket::call() (app/Models/Ticket.php:115). Deactivation, per-entity slug uniqueness including the race catch, and the inactive-queue/authorization ordering are implemented.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes go through actions, authorization through the policy, the migration is generated-style with a reversible down() (database/migrations/2026_10_29_032643_create_queue_access_table.php:28-31), QueueAccess declares Fillable (app/Models/QueueAccess.php:11), and docs/CHANGELOG were updated. One doc-sync miss: docs/business-rules.md:118 still says Ticket::call() is 'entity-membership checked' and that 'AuthZ stays out of scope per #20', contradicting the new policy-based call authorization.

security.evidence: Every write/call path authorizes server-side before mutating: CreateQueue (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:18), UpdateQueue (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:35), SetQueueAccess (app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:36), CallNextTicket (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:32), and Ticket::call() (app/Models/Ticket.php:115). Names/slugs are validated, SetQueueAccess rejects unknown/non-string permissions and cross-entity memberships, and QueuePolicy::call denies corrupted non-array permission values with an is_array() check plus strict in_array().

tests.evidence: The suite covers the main paths and failure/authorization paths: CreateQueueTest, UpdateQueueTest, SetQueueAccessTest, QueuePolicyTest, and new CallNextTicket/Ticket::call tests, including every CallMode (tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php:825-842) and corrupted grant values (tests/Feature/QueuePolicyTest.php:1089-1100). Two edge gaps remain: the queue-FK cascade is not tested (tests/Feature/SetQueueAccessTest.php:151 only deletes the membership), and the UpdateQueue race-conversion branch (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:59-66) has no test.

simplicity.evidence: Reuses the existing actions/models, shares normalization in one small trait (app/Actions/Concerns/NormalizesQueueFields.php), and adds no service/repository layer or speculative abstraction; SetQueueAccess uses the existing transaction/upsert facilities.

readability.evidence: Names and docblocks are clear and methods are focused, but UpdateQueue returns the caller's model after setRawAttributes() (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:68), a surprising input mutation, and the race catch re-normalizes the slug, which takes a second read.

scope.evidence: Every change serves the queue/access/call-authorization task; existing CallNextTicketTest actors were updated only where the new authorization required it, and docs/tests are the required supporting changes. No UI, extra permissions, or queue deletion was added.

issues.explanation: The retained 'Single-ticket call (scope note)' still says Ticket::call() is 'entity-membership checked' and that 'AuthZ stays out of scope per #20', which contradicts the new QueuePolicy::call enforcement documented just above it.

The test named 'cascades grants when the queue or membership is deleted' deletes only the membership, so the queue_id cascade from the migration is never exercised; rename the test or add a queue-deletion assertion.
The QueryException-to-ValidationException race branch in UpdateQueue has no test, unlike CreateQueue's race test, so the update slug-race behavior is unverified.
Returning the caller's $queue after setRawAttributes() mutates the input model as a side effect; returning $updated or documenting the mutation would be clearer.

The 'offers no way to delete a queue' test greps action filenames for Delete/Remove/Destroy and would fail for any unrelated future action with that name, e.g. a ticket action; a narrower queue-behavior assertion would be less brittle.

review.summary: The change implements the queue lifecycle, per-queue access grants, QueuePolicy, and call-path authorization, with updated docs and a broad Pest suite. Functionally it meets the task; the main follow-ups are the stale Ticket::call() paragraph in business-rules, a few untested edges (queue-delete cascade and the UpdateQueue race branch), and the surprising input-model mutation in UpdateQueue. Approve with nits.
